🇧🇪

Belgium

27 ads · €5315 spend · 193 purchases
✅ What's Working
• WCDxBA concept is the efficiency engine — three variants all profitable (#5 at 10.3x, #1 at 5.11x, #2 at 3.45x) with CPPs under €28, proving this creative angle resonates deeply in BE.
• Diamond Earstud #4 is a hidden monster: 12.71x ROAS and €7.47 CPP on just €37 spend — the best ad in the account is criminally underfunded.
• The lone carousel (Carousel_120237873305580396 - Copy) outperforms most statics at volume: 5.39x ROAS, €17.95 CPP, 44 purchases — format is underexploited with only one live.
❌ What's Not Working
• Heart concepts have a conversion problem, not a click problem: Heart Tag #1 burns €351 at 0.77x ROAS despite 177% CTR, Heart Catalog #1 same pattern at 184% CTR but 1.06x ROAS — creatives attract attention but the product or landing page kills the sale.
• Solitaire concept is dead on arrival: #1 manages only 1.96x with the account's lowest CTR (68.91%), #2 spent €44 for literally zero purchases.
• Split concept is a slow bleed: #1 is the worst performer in the account at 0.43x ROAS (€128 CPP), #2 barely scrapes 2.02x — neither justifies further investment.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more WCDxBA variants immediately — this concept converts consistently across every iteration tested; create #3, #4, and explore video/carousel formats for it.
• Scale Diamond Earstud aggressively and build a product-hero mini-franchise around it — at 12.71x ROAS this product clearly has exceptional product-market fit in Belgium.
• Expand carousel format across all proven concepts (Summer, WCDxBA, Diamond Earstud) — only one carousel exists and it's the second-highest ROAS ad at meaningful spend.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the entire Solitaire concept — two variants, zero evidence of viability, €207 wasted.
• Kill Split #1 immediately — 0.43x ROAS is lighting money on fire. Demote Split #2 to life support at best.
• Kill Heart Tag #1 and Heart Catalog #1 — high CTR with sub-1.1x ROAS means the creative promises something the product page doesn't deliver. Fix the funnel or stop promoting these products.

🇩🇪

Germany

3 ads · €553 spend · 3 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Video _ Kay #1 is the only ad showing any purchase signal (ROAS 1.46x, CPP €82.79) — Kay concept has legs.
• Video format outperforms static on purchase conversion in this market — both video ads generated purchases, static did not.
• CTR is strong across all three ads, meaning the brand and product resonate visually with German audiences — the funnel breaks post-click, not pre-click.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video _ Stack #1 burned €349 for a single purchase at ROAS 0.26x — this is the top-spend ad and it's destroying the account's efficiency.
• Static _ Earstud New #1 has zero purchases on €38 spend — too early to kill but static format is not converting in DE.
• Overall creative volume is dangerously thin: only 3 ads means the algorithm has almost nothing to optimize against. Germany is being starved of creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Kay concept in multiple formats — UGC, carousel, new hooks. It's the only proven converter; exhaust it before moving on.
• Video-first creative strategy for DE. Both purchases came from video; lean into motion, styling, and on-body content.
• German-language or German-localized creative. Three English-origin ads in a non-English market likely explains the post-click drop-off despite high CTR.

Kamping Kitsch Club — Ads Report

24 August 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads + Google Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

30 ads · €3601 spend · 1290 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Urgency statics are the profit engine: 'Last Call' series averages 51x ROAS with CPPs between €0.65–€1.60 — bottom-funnel scarcity messaging crushes everything else in the account.
• Price-anchoring and value-framing statics convert hard: 'Static _ Berekening #2' hits 39.26x ROAS, 'Static _ Goedkoopste #1 - Copy' at 18.3x, and 'Waar vo' variants at 20–31x ROAS — rational purchase justification works on this Belgian audience.
• Artist-specific callouts outperform generic branding: 'Static _ RUBEN' delivers 27x ROAS at €2.65 CPP, proving that a name + face + bold claim beats vague festival hype.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video aftermovie is a conversion killer: 'Video _ Aftermovie #1' delivers €17.69 CPP — 10 to 27x worse than top statics on comparable spend. The assumed 'video-first' creative strategy is flatly wrong for purchase campaigns.
• Organic repurposed content fails at paid: 'Static _ Organic #1' is the only money-losing ad in the account at 0.94x ROAS and €36.68 CPP — organic posts do not translate to paid performance.
• Budget allocation is inverted: 'Static _ Hart #2' gets €653 at 23.69x while 'Static _ Last Call #1 - Copy' gets €75 at 78.75x ROAS — the best ads are starved and the good-but-not-great ads eat the budget.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3–5 new urgency/scarcity static variants — rotate hooks like 'Laatste 100 tickets', 'Bijna uitverkocht', '24u resterend' to combat fatigue on the Last Call format that prints money at sub-€1 CPP.
• Build an artist spotlight static template from the RUBEN ad and produce one for every major lineup act — name, photo, one punchy claim, ticket CTA. Systematize what's already working at 27x ROAS.
• Expand price-comparison and value-calculation statics — the Berekening (39x ROAS) and Goedkoopste (18x ROAS) concepts tap into rational justification; create variants comparing festival cost to a night out, streaming subscriptions, or other festivals.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running aftermovie videos in conversion campaigns immediately — €17.69 CPP is indefensible when statics deliver €0.65. Relegate video to reach/awareness campaigns only.
• Pause all organic-repurposed creatives in paid — 'Organic #1' at 0.94x is literally losing money. What works organically is not paid creative.
• Stop distributing budget evenly across all ads. Redirect 70%+ of spend into the Last Call, Berekening, RUBEN, and Code formats that are proven converters.

Belgium

30 ads · €9687 spend · 267 results
✅ What's Working
• Comparison (Vergelijking) statics dominate: 'Static _ Vergelijking #1 - Copy' variants hit €15–25/result across ad sets, generating 94 leads on ~€2,194 combined spend — the savings-vs-broker angle clearly resonates with Belgian homeowners.
• 'Static _ Smart #1 - Copy' (€335 variant) is the stealth winner at €18.61/result with 18 leads — whatever this creative does differently is working hard.
• Static formats categorically outperform video: best statics deliver €15–25/result while video averages €42–69/result. The audience wants to read the value prop, not watch it.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Static _ De Tijd 2' spent €232 for zero results — press/authority positioning isn't converting. The copy of this ad ('De Tijd 2 - Copy') somehow works at €26.28, suggesting the original creative execution is broken, not the angle.
• Engagement-bait formats flop: 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' at €85.75/result and 'Static _ Product #2 - Copy' at €117.60/result — these cost 3–5x your best performers.
• One 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' variant blew €265 on a single lead (€264.61) while the other Copy 2 ran fine at €38.68 — audience or placement targeting issue, not creative.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce 3–4 new Vergelijking #1 iterations: test different fee examples (€300K home, €400K home), side-by-side visual layouts, and regional pricing to keep the comparison angle fresh before fatigue hits.
• Scale the Smart format aggressively — the €18.61 variant proves this template converts; create Smart #2 and #3 with different hooks (zero-risk guarantee, 40% more buyers, Immoweb listing quality).
• Invest in calculator/savings statics: 'Static _ Berekening #1' at €30.96/result with minimal spend shows the 'how much do you save' angle has untapped potential — build a series with concrete euro amounts.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all poll-format creatives immediately — 'Static _ Poll #2 - Copy 2' at €85.75/result is burning budget on engagement that doesn't convert to leads.
• Pause 'Static _ Product #2 - Copy' (€117.60/result) and the broken 'Static _ Vergelijking #2 - Copy 2' (€264.61/result) — these are pure waste.
• Stop investing in 'General Video #1 - Copy' variants — both copies run €55–69/result. Video isn't earning its keep; reallocate that budget to proven static formats.

AI

Creative Analysis

20 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

20 ads · €361 spend · 34 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Scarcity and countdown messaging is the clear winner — "Video _ Tickets Countdown #4" delivered 32.73x ROAS at €1.99 CPP, and "Video _ Urgency #3" drove 14 purchases at 8.05x ROAS on the highest spend.
• Broad/general creative converts efficiently — "Video _ General 3" returned 5.15x ROAS without needing a specific lineup hook.
• Early static urgency signals are electric — "Static _ Urgency #6" and "Static _ Paradisco Key Visual #1" both converted on near-zero spend with absurd ROAS, suggesting Meta's algo hasn't even begun to unlock them.
❌ What's Not Working
• Lineup-specific ads are a money pit — "Video _ Saturday Lineup #1" burned €88 for a single purchase (0.58x ROAS), and both Friday Lineup ads (€32 combined) generated zero purchases. Audiences don't care about lineup info in ad format.
• Aftermovie creative underdelivers on conversions — "Video _ Aftermovie #1" scraped one sale, and #2 and #3 got virtually no spend or results. Too much brand, not enough buy-now pressure.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more countdown/scarcity video variants — this is the highest-converting concept by a wide margin. Test different countdown windows (72h, 24h, final hours) and visual treatments.
• Scale static urgency concepts — the statics that converted show the format works for impulse-buy ticket messaging. Create a rapid-fire batch of 5+ statics with countdown copy, price anchors, and sold-out-soon framing.
• Build hybrid creatives: aftermovie footage recut with urgency overlays and CTAs — combine the emotional pull of event footage with the scarcity hook that actually drives purchases.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all lineup-focused ads immediately. Three lineup ads, €120 spent, one conversion. The data is clear — lineup reveals don't sell tickets in-feed.
• Stop running pure aftermovie content as conversion ads. They're awareness pieces being forced into a conversion objective. Use them as raw footage for urgency edits instead.

Meta Ads + Google Ads + Klaviyo Email · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

14 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🇧🇪

Belgium

10 ads · €3643 spend · 56 purchases
✅ What's Working
• Static formats dominate: every static ad converts, while two Sieben Split videos returned zero purchases. Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy (4.42x) and Static _ Offer #3 (8.46x) prove lifestyle imagery + offer hooks crush video in this market.
• Offer-led creatives are the revenue engine: the three Offer statics combined delivered 28 purchases at ~2.3x blended ROAS — price/promo messaging clearly resonates against Oakley/Decathlon positioning.
• UGC outperforms polished creator video: Video _ Sieben UGC #1 (€51.15 CPP, 1.95x ROAS) beats both the scripted Sieben Item (€63.62 CPP) and Renée (€96.17 CPP) videos handily.
❌ What's Not Working
• Video _ Renée #1 - Copy is a cash incinerator: €577 spent for just 1.01x ROAS and €96 CPP — highest cost per purchase in the account by 50%. Whatever this creative is doing, the audience rejects it.
• Sieben Split format is dead on arrival: both Split #1 and Split #2 burned €131 combined with zero purchases. Split-screen comparison or multi-scene format fails to convert.
• Video creative overall lags statics: 4 of 5 videos sit below 2x ROAS while 4 of 5 statics sit at or above 2x. The brand is over-investing in video relative to performance.
⬆ Double Down On
• Lifestyle statics with subtle offer overlays — Static _ Lifestyle #2 - Copy proves aspirational in-action imagery converts at 4.42x with €29 CPP; produce 3-5 variants across cycling/running/ski contexts.
• Hard offer statics — Static _ Offer #3 hit 8.46x at tiny spend; scale it and create fresh offer angles (bundle deals, 'op sterkte' upgrade pricing, seasonal hooks).
• Raw UGC statics and short clips from real Belgian riders/runners — the Sieben UGC direction works but polished creator content does not; lean into authenticity over production value.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the Sieben Split format immediately — two ads, zero purchases, the concept fails.
• Pause Video _ Renée #1 - Copy now — 1.01x ROAS at €577 is subsidizing Meta, not NAOS.
• Stop producing high-production creator videos until a video concept proves it can beat your cheapest static (€29 CPP). The data says statics win.

🇧🇪

Belgium

4 ads · €817 spend · 68 results
✅ What's Working
• 'Static _ Investeren _ 2' is carrying the entire market single-handedly — 68 leads at €11.62 is strong for real estate lead gen, proving the investment angle resonates with Belgian audiences.
• Static format with an investment hook clearly connects — the combination of financial appeal and Zeeland waterfront positioning is landing.
• The algorithm has spoken: it consolidated nearly all budget (€790 of €817) into the one winner, confirming creative-level signal is strong on that variant.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero creative diversity — every single ad is an 'Investeren' static. No lifestyle angle, no second-home dreaming, no kijkwoning visit CTA, no video. You're fishing with one lure in a lake full of different fish.
• 'Static _ Investeren _ 3' burned €22 with zero results and a comparatively weak 66.83% CTR — it failed to earn its way into rotation and should be considered dead weight.
• Variants _ 4 and the original 'Static _ Investeren' never got enough spend to prove anything (€3 and €2), suggesting Meta's algorithm rejected them instantly against the _2 winner.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more investment-angle variations — different hooks, numbers, urgency triggers — to find a second winner and reduce single-ad dependency before fatigue hits 'Static _ Investeren _ 2.'
• Launch lifestyle and emotional creatives: Westerschelde sunsets, panoramic views from the apartment, the feeling of rust and ruimte — tap the second-home dreamer audience you're currently ignoring entirely.
• Create kijkwoning-specific ads with a clear visit CTA — this is the campaign's stated conversion goal yet no ad explicitly drives showroom visits.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running four near-identical 'Investeren' statics and hoping the algorithm sorts it out — it already did, and three lost.
• Kill the illusion that static-only, investment-only messaging is a complete strategy — you're leaving the lifestyle buyer and second-home seeker completely untouched.

Other

17 ads · €3968 spend · 331 results
✅ What's Working
• 'Water Wind _ Form' is the clear winner — 150 leads at €8.80 CPR with highest spend, proving emotional water/wind imagery paired with instant forms converts at scale.
• 'Visit #2 - Copy' delivers the cheapest leads at €7.87 CPR across 75 results — the kijkwoning visit CTA is a natural low-friction ask for real estate.
• Efficient mid-tier performers 'Video #2' (€9.42), 'Nieuw_App #1' (€9.60), and 'Aanbod Tag #1' (€10.76) show that product-specific creative with clear offers converts — they just need more budget to prove scale.
❌ What's Not Working
• 'Dreamer #1' and 'Dreamer #2' are zero-result duds (€90 combined, 0 leads) — pure aspirational lifestyle without a concrete hook doesn't convert in this funnel. Dreamy doesn't mean vague.
• 'Opsomming' bullet-list formats flopped — #2 cost €38.03/result and #1 got zero leads. Feature dumps kill desire in a lifestyle-driven category.
• 'Review _ Form' at €28.35 CPR on €794 spend is a quiet budget drain — social proof alone isn't enough to drive action, needs pairing with a stronger offer or visit CTA.
⬆ Double Down On
• Water/nature emotional imagery + instant form combo — replicate the 'Water Wind' formula with new visuals (sunset, tides, aerial Westerschelde shots) and always pair with lead forms.
• Kijkwoning visit CTAs — 'Visit #2 - Copy' proves this is the sharpest conversion hook. Create urgency variants (limited weekends, new phase openings, seasonal angles).
• Short video with specific product focus — 'Video #2' at €9.42 CPR signals video works when it's product-grounded, not just mood. Produce more 15-second property walkthroughs and view reveals.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill the 'Dreamer' concept entirely — zero conversions, pure waste. Aspirational without specificity is wallpaper.
• Kill 'Opsomming' bullet-point formats — feature lists actively repel this audience. Nobody falls in love with a spec sheet.
• Slash 'Review _ Form' budget immediately — at 3.2x the CPR of your best ads, it's burning money for mediocre leads.

14 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no purch.

🌐

Other

14 ads · €369 spend · 1 purchases
✅ What's Working
• "Instagram post: New deliveries! Bekijk ons gamma..." is the only ad generating revenue — 10.66x ROAS at €79.71 CPP. Product catalog / range messaging converts.
• CTRs across the board are absurdly inflated (likely engagement/link clicks on low-spend posts), but the highest-CTR ads like "shop online" (633.80%) and "New!! Delivery winter 2026" (598.71%) show audience curiosity for newness and seasonal drops.
• Dutch/bilingual copy ("Bekijk ons gamma") resonates — the only converting ad uses it.
❌ What's Not Working
• 13 out of 14 ads produced zero purchases — €291 burned with nothing to show. Ads like "Bericht: ''" (3 variants, €42 total) have blank copy and zero conversions.
• Event-style ads ("Early bird start of the season days!") and emoji-only posts ("❤️", "🦆 KLAAR VOOR DE OPENING") drive no purchases despite decent CTR — engagement without intent.
• Spend is spread too thin across 14 ads with tiny budgets (€0–€80). No ad gets enough budget to exit learning phase or optimize properly.
⬆ Double Down On
• Product catalog / new arrivals messaging in Dutch with clear shopping CTA — replicate the "Bekijk ons gamma" formula with different product categories.
• Seasonal collection drops with specific product imagery and prices — the audience clicks on newness, now close the sale.
• Consolidate budget into 3-4 ads max to exit learning phase and let Meta's algorithm optimize for purchase conversions.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running ads with blank or emoji-only copy — "Bericht: ''" and "❤️" are vanity engagement traps with zero commercial value.
• Stop spreading €370/month across 14 micro-budget ads. Consolidation is non-negotiable.
• Stop boosting Instagram posts without purchase-optimized campaign structure — these are content promotion, not performance ads.

✅ What's Working
• Abnormally high CTRs (119%+ on 120239393986810631, 111%+ on 120239394435940631) suggest strong curiosity and click intent — people want to engage.
• The brand clearly generates interest in-feed; creative hooks are compelling enough to earn multiple clicks per impression.
❌ What's Not Working
• Zero results across both ads despite €90 total spend — every euro is burning with no tracked conversion. 120239393986810631 has €86 wasted.
• CTRs over 100% are a massive red flag: likely broken pixel, misconfigured conversion event, or a landing page that kills all intent. Clicks are happening but nothing registers downstream.
• No creative variation exists — only 2 ads total means zero learning about what converts, just two versions of the same black hole.
⬆ Double Down On
• Fix the funnel first: audit pixel, CAPI setup, and landing page before any new spend — clicks prove demand exists.
• Lean into B2B workwear pain points (safety compliance, team branding, bulk pricing) with direct-response creative built for lead gen.
• Test Dutch-language UGC or testimonial-style ads showing real Belgian businesses in EVN workwear — social proof is king in B2B.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop running any ads until conversion tracking is confirmed functional — you are flying blind and bleeding budget.
• Kill the assumption that clicks = performance. 119% CTR with 0 results means the problem is post-click, not pre-click.

• Calculator lead magnets crush it — "Plat dak | Calculator" delivers leads at €13.46 vs €27-33 for non-calculator hellend dak ads. The interactive cost tool clearly converts.
• Plat dak outperforms hellend dak across the board: 75 results vs 38-42 at nearly half the CPR. Flat roof homeowners are a hotter audience.

⬆ Double Down On
• Calculator-style lead magnets for every roof type and angle — this interactive value-first approach is your best-performing format by far.
• Plat dak targeting deserves 2-3x the budget of hellend dak given the CPR gap (€13.46 vs €27-33). Shift budget aggressively.
• Recruitment via Meta is working — expand the "Vacature" playbook to other roles while CPR stays under €5.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Stop scaling "Asbestvrij dak" without a creative refresh — at €32.93/lead it's 2.4x worse than the plat dak calculator.
• Kill the assumption that hellend dak and plat dak deserve equal budgets. The data screams plat dak. Reallocate.

🌐

Other

30 ads · €8440 spend · 122 results
✅ What's Working
• Vottem project dominates: Vottem_apt (€13.80/result), Vottem_video (€22.70, 24 results), and Vottem_animatie (€33.11) all deliver strong volume at low cost — video/animation formats clearly resonate.
• Brugge_penthouse is a quiet monster: 19 results at €40.62 with a 361% CTR — high engagement, strong conversion, and room to scale.
• Georges v2 iteration worked: georges_image_CTA_v2 (€47.74/result, 5 results) outperforms v1 (€271.73, 1 result) by 5.7x — proving iterative CTA testing pays off.
❌ What's Not Working
• Wildebeek is a money pit across every format: slideshow (€562/result), flexibele units (€322 spent, 0 results), reel (€168.78/result), rem (€229/result) — the project or creative angle is fundamentally broken.
• Charleroi_te-huur burned €332 for 1 result and has the lowest CTR in the account (57.95%) — rental messaging or audience is off.
• Stokerie ads get high CTR but terrible conversion: stokerie_terras (140% CTR, €95.46/result) and stokerie_int_v2 (€117.44/result) — clicks aren't translating, likely a landing page or offer mismatch.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more Vottem creative variants: video and animation formats at this project deliver sub-€35 results consistently — test new angles, unit types, lifestyle hooks.
• Replicate the Brugge_penthouse formula for other premium units: penthouse/luxury positioning with high-engagement creative clearly works — apply to Georges, Blom, and Stokerie.
• Scale the v2 CTA iteration approach: the Georges v1→v2 improvement was dramatic — systematically A/B test CTA copy and placement across all active projects.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all Wildebeek ads immediately: 4 ads, €1,282 total spend, 3 results combined — this project has no viable creative angle running.
• Kill Charleroi_te-huur: rental positioning at €332/result is unsustainable — either the audience or the offer needs a total rethink before any more spend.
• Kill ODD Vottem 22/8: €150 spent, 0 results — even in the strong Vottem project, this format/approach failed.

MULTI COMPTE — Ads Report

24 August 2026 · Last 30 days

Meta Ads · Creative insights + Performance

AI

Creative Analysis

30 ads · Meta · last 30 days

Split by country · Click any card → public post · Green border = ROAS ≥3 · Yellow = ROAS ≥1.5 · Red = no results

🌐

Other

30 ads · €7910 spend · 290 results
✅ What's Working
• Carousel format for pergolas is the engine: PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_MUTLI4 variants consistently deliver €20-22 CPR across three ad sets, with the top variant pulling 99 results at €22.22 — best volume-to-efficiency ratio in the account.
• Video creative punches above its weight: VERANDA VERANCOBEL - VIDEO delivers €19.27 CPR (30 results) and PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3 hits €23.06 CPR — video is the only format making PVC even remotely viable.
• Conversion-optimized veranda copy works: VERANDAS - PUB CONVERTIONS - Copie at €18.01 CPR (25 results) is the cheapest lead in the entire account.
❌ What's Not Working
• PVC product line is a money pit: PVC VERANCOBEL (€95.91 and €66.37 CPR), PUB PVC 3 (€68.42 CPR) — combined €367 spent for just 5 leads. The product category lacks creative-market fit.
• 'PUB' static-style ads consistently underperform their carousel/video counterparts: PUB PERGOLAS 2 (€35.83), PUB CARPORT 1 (€59.55), PUB VERANDAS 2 (€0 results twice for €156 burned).
• PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 ate €782 for only 9 results (€86.83 CPR) — 4x worse than MUTLI4 carousel with identical product. Audience or creative is broken.
⬆ Double Down On
• Produce more carousel variants for pergolas and extend the format to carports and verandas — MUTLI4 proves the template works, now replicate it across product lines.
• Scale video creative aggressively: VERANDA VIDEO and PVCS_VIDEO_MUTLI3 show video is the strongest format for engagement and conversion — every product line needs a video variant.
• Double budget on the €18-20 CPR winners (VERANDAS CONVERTIONS Copie, CARPORTS €729 variant, MAQUETTE PERGOLAS) — these are under-invested relative to their efficiency.
🛑 Kill or Rethink
• Kill all PVC static ads immediately (PVC VERANCOBEL both variants, PUB PVC 3) — €367 for 5 leads is indefensible. If PVC must run, video-only.
• Kill PUB VERANDAS 2 (both ad sets: €156 total, zero results) and PUB CARPORT 1 (€60, 1 result) — 'PUB' format is dead.
• Kill PERGOLA_CARROUSEL_RJF7 — at €86.83 CPR next to MUTLI4 at €22.22, this is the same product with 4x worse performance. No reason to keep it alive.
